newsitem.title: USA: Zebra says ends retail software business.
newsitem.headline: Zebra says ends retail software business.

text.p: Zebra Technologies Corp said it closed its retail software business, resulting in a $0.10 per share charge against second-quarter earnings.
"We simply could not justify the continued heavy investment in developing the PC retail channel," said chief financial officer Charles Whitchurch.

The maker of products used in bar code applications on Tuesday reported second-quarter net income, after the charge, of $7.2 million, or $0.30 per share, on sales of $47.8 million. In the same period a year ago, net income was $6.3 million, or $0.26 per share, on sales of $38.9 million.
Zebra said gross margins increased on the quarter to 50.8 percent thanks to cost reductions a favorable sales mix.
Shares in the company closed Tuesday up 1 to 30-1/8.
